name: CMOS Ring Oscillator — Odd-Stage Inverter Loop
description: Odd-stage feedback inverter chain. Each stage is a CMOS inverter (PMOS + NMOS). The feedback from the last stage to the first creates 360° phase shift (each inverter contributes 180°, the odd count ensures net inversion). Oscillation frequency = 1/(2·N·t_pd) where N is the stage count and t_pd is the per-stage propagation delay.

Low Leakage.reasoning: Increased channel length L=0.35um reduces subthreshold leakage; frequency decreases due to higher t_pd.

Low Power.reasoning: Longer channels and standard widths: minimal switching power, acceptable jitter for clock reference use.

High Speed.reasoning: Minimum length L=0.15um and wide channels (3x standard) minimise t_pd for maximum oscillation frequency.

default.reasoning: Standard SKY130 inverter sizing; symmetric rise/fall times, good jitter performance.

sizing_notes.M_P{i}: Inverter PMOS stage i — wider than NMOS to compensate lower hole mobility; ensures symmetric duty cycle.
sizing_notes.M_N{i}: Inverter NMOS stage i — baseline reference width; propagation delay is primarily determined by this device.
